title: Runtime discovery walks to the nearest .memory-seed
decision: Runtime discovery uses nearest-ancestor `.memory-seed/` directory, walking upward from current working directory to find the active runtime.
why: Canonical runtime location enables portable memory systems and supports nested sub-project runtimes with automatic scoping.
evolution: Founded from the control file; no session lineage attached yet.
source_quote: Runtime discovery walks upward from `cwd` and uses the nearest `.memory-seed/`.

title: Control-file authority partition (index/policy/skills/sessions)
decision: Authority for project topology, active state, and behavioral constraints is partitioned across four files: `index.md` (state and topology), `policy.md` (constraints), `skills/` (execution runbooks), and `sessions/` (chronological history).
why: Separation of concerns makes each file discoverable and maintainable. `index.md` combines topology and priorities; `policy.md` contains constraints only; routing files expose the runtime to agents.
evolution: Founded from the control file; no session lineage attached yet.
source_quote: `index.md` combines topology, active state, durable project context, current priorities, workflows, risks, inheritance, and skill activation.

supporting.quote: `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `GEMINI.md` route tools into the shared runtime.

title: Sub-project runtime scoping and inheritance defaults
decision: Sub-projects are normal folders with their own `.memory-seed/` directory that is not nested inside the root. Policy is inherited by default; skills inherit by default unless overridden locally.
why: Nearest-runtime discovery scopes work under each `.memory-seed/`, and inheritance defaults reduce duplication while allowing local customization.
evolution: Founded from the control file; no session lineage attached yet.
source_quote: Sub-projects live as normal folders with their own `.memory-seed/`; they are not nested inside the root `.memory-seed/`.

supporting.quote: A nested `.memory-seed/` runtime scopes work under its containing folder.

title: Four never-merged edge kinds, forward-only and acyclic
decision: Lifecycle edges comprise four never-merged kinds: `replaces`, `evolves`, `related_entries`, and `evolved_by` (inverse). Edges are forward-only and acyclic by contract.
why: Four independent relationship claims deserve distinct semantic labels. Forward-only and acyclic structure ensures the edge graph is append-only and prevents cycles in artifact lineage.
evolution: Founded from the control file; no session lineage attached yet.
source_quote: Evolution edges and artifact lineage (core shipped in 2.18.0; Trace continuity completed 2026-07-15): typed `evolves:` plus read-time `evolved_by`, inverse-field and continuity validation

title: Append-only link retraction via retracts: blocks
decision: A published lifecycle edge is downgraded or removed through a new `retracts:` block appended to the same sidecar file, never by editing the published block in place. A downgrade is a retract of the old kind plus a fresh edge of the new kind.
why: Append-only architecture forbids in-place edits to published history. Retraction blocks provide an explicit, auditable correction mechanism that preserves the original edge and the correction.
evolution: Founded from the control file; no session lineage attached yet.
source_quote: Append-only link retraction (current unreleased worktree, 2026-07-25): a published lifecycle edge is downgraded or removed via a NEW `retracts: <kind> <ref>` block

title: edge_confidence on machine-suggested edges; consumers fade low tiers
decision: Machine-suggested lifecycle edges carry a structured `edge_confidence` field with confidence tier (`low`, `review`, `high`). Consumers fade low-confidence edges by opacity; the graph offers a threshold filter.
why: Distinguishing authored edges from machine-suggested ones with confidence tiers makes the provenance transparent and lets readers see which relationships require human verification.

title: Topic sidecar is the topic authority (sidecar > authored > hashtag)
decision: Topics are resolved in precedence order: topic sidecar (authoritative), authored entry-level topics, then hashtags (fallback). Sidecar is the source of truth for decision-level topic attribution.
why: A dedicated sidecar family for decision-level topics enables fine-grained topic attribution and provides a clean, explicit override point for curation.
evolution: Founded from the control file; no session lineage attached yet.
source_quote: **The topic sidecar is now the topic authority, not a derived overlay**: a fourth sidecar family declares `area:`/`activity:` per DECISION, and `_topics()` reads sidecar → authored → hashtag in that precedence

title: Derived never implicitly overrides write-time
decision: A `derived` sidecar block may never implicitly override a `write-time` block on recency alone; it may only fill a gap. Explicit override requires a human-reviewed `retracts:` naming the block it supersedes.
why: Protecting authored intent against silent machine override preserves the authority of human judgment. Explicit retraction keeps every correction auditable.
evolution: Founded from the control file; no session lineage attached yet.
source_quote: General precedence rule across sidecar families (Constitution v1.6, 2026-07-26): a `derived` block may never *implicitly* override a `write-time` block on recency alone — it may only fill a gap.

title: Scored topic auto-backfill rejected; curated-evidence premise adopted
decision: Automated topic backfill with scoring gates is rejected. Manual, curated attribution is adopted: one worker per batch judges all decision units and writes final topic assignments without automated scoring.
why: Two pilot runs scored macro-recall at 58.3% and 61.3% against a 0.70 gate, falling short. The curated-evidence premise succeeded: a human worker with swarm output as evidence judged 1,030 units and wrote 2,013 attributions (95% carrying both axes).
evolution: Founded from the control file; no session lineage attached yet.
source_quote: Decision-level topic judgment swarm — **the scored auto-backfill was piloted twice and explicitly ABORTED (2026-07-26)**: two pilot runs scored macro-recall 0.583 and 0.613 against a 0.70 gate
